context: Ticket 4821. Customer: Orchard Bakery, contact Lena Brook. Problem: checkout shows error 500 since the update on Tuesday. The payment plugin PayFlow was updated from 3.9 to 4.2. Site runs PHP 8.1. A backup runs every night at 3 AM. The hosting plan includes 3 support hours per month. Failed orders in the log so far: 5.

lines.text: Hi Lena, this is Dan from support. I have your ticket in front of me.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Thank you for calling back so fast. Our checkout is broken and it is the busiest week of the year for us.
I understand. Let me ask a few questions and look at the logs while we talk.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Sure. Tom is next to me, he saw it first.
Tom, what did you see when you tried to pay on the site?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: A white page with an error 500 right after clicking pay.
Okay, thanks. Lena, when did the problem begin?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: It began on Monday, right after the update.
My ticket says the update ran on Tuesday, let me check that.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Oh, maybe Tuesday then. It was a crazy week. First of all, is my data safe?
Your data is safe. There is a nightly backup, and we can restore from it if needed.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Good. And I need to know what is causing this, because last time you said it was fixed and it was not.
You are right to be careful. This time we will confirm the fix together with a test order.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Okay. So what is the cause?
It looks like the payment plugin update. I am reading the error log to confirm.
I see the PayFlow plugin went from version 3.9 to 4.2 on the update day.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Is that bad? What is a plugin version anyway, and why does it matter for PHP?
The site runs PHP 8.1, and the new plugin version may not fully support it.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: We had three orders fail since this morning, I think.
The log shows five failed orders so far. I will list them for you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Lena, did you call the delivery guy about tomorrow?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Not yet, Tom, please do that now.
While Tom calls, I will roll the plugin back to version 3.9 on a copy of the site first.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Do you think it will be fixed in an hour?
I cannot promise an hour yet. Let me finish the test on the copy.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Fine. Do I need to pay extra for this work?
This falls under your support hours, and I will confirm the hours used at the end.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Another thing. Our emails to customers also stopped working since yesterday.
Let me note the email problem and finish the checkout first.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Okay. By the way, I will send you a screenshot of the error in ten minutes.
Great, thank you. I will tell you as soon as the copy test is done.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I also need to tell my customers something. What should I post on our page?
I can write a short notice for you to post while we fix it.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And our site runs PHP 7.4, right? Tom said so last month.
The ticket says PHP 8.1, so that matches the cause we are looking at.
I will update you every half hour until it is solved.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: And one more question, will we lose the orders that failed?
The failed orders are saved in the log, and I can send you the list to contact them.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Please do. Dan, can you send me the log file?
I will send it with the summary.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Lena, the delivery guy says tomorrow morning is fine.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Great. Thanks Tom.
The copy is ready. I am rolling back the plugin now.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Dan, is it working? What happens if the rollback fails?
If the rollback fails, we restore from last night's backup, so nothing is lost.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I tried a test order on the copy link you sent and it went through.
Perfect. Then I will apply the same rollback on the live site and we test together.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Please. And tell me what we do about the new version later.
We should wait for a plugin release that works with PHP 8.1 before updating again.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Sounds right. Call me when it is live.
I will call you as soon as it is live. Thanks Lena.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Thank you Dan.
